> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 29c7157af4fed4738b3da14bbfb008496cbd1f6a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b00d0fbf6dbc3b58c4a3318c8c6a5874cd0b332c` — the merge of head `6cf223708fd4222dc97ed137e50f48c7c0f2d97b` into base `29c7157af4fed4738b3da14bbfb008496cbd1f6a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b00d0fbf6dbc3b58c4a3318c8c6a5874cd0b332c && git checkout b00d0fbf6dbc3b58c4a3318c8c6a5874cd0b332c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 29c7157af4fed4738b3da14bbfb008496cbd1f6a 6cf223708fd4222dc97ed137e50f48c7c0f2d97b && git checkout -B drift-repro 29c7157af4fed4738b3da14bbfb008496cbd1f6a && git merge --no-ff 6cf223708fd4222dc97ed137e50f48c7c0f2d97b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 29c7157af4fed4738b3da14bbfb008496cbd1f6a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than

> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 29c7157af4fed4738b3da14bbfb008496cbd1f6a` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6cf223708fd4222dc97ed137e50f48c7c0f2d97b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/objectql/src/protocol-sentinel-owner-draft-save-address.test.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts (unboundItemDraftAddress, resolveWriteHead, put), packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (the DELETE door's state and package query), .changeset/23712-draft-save-d99-address.md, .changeset/23514-sentinel-owner-save.md on main, docs/adr/0029, docs/adr/0048, docs/adr/0070

Read: card #23712 (body, triage 6199836399, the two state comments, claim 6204753931, dispatch 6204788515, the os-dev-report 6205514662 with its 36-cell draft_save_matrix), PR #23769 (body, file list, the net diff against the merge base 2906cd8d2e, which holds a869ea6362 and c03077e294 as ancestors), the head's 39 check-runs, and at the head the whole of `saveMetaItem`'s D9.9 block, `unboundOwnerPackageRefusal` with its arm order, `UnboundOwnerRefusalState`, `classifyObjectContribution`, `packagelessAddress`, `packagelessDraftAddress`, the promote door's and the registry write-through's calls of `overlayPackageMismatchError`, `deleteMetaItem`'s draft-discard address, `isSealedManagedItem` / `refusePackagedBaseOverride`, and in the repository `unboundItemDraftAddress`, `resolveWriteHead` and `put`. Judged against ADR-0029 D3 (one owner per object name) and D9.9 (a row bound to a package that does not own the object is refused at the producer, loudly, so `sys_metadata` never describes a shape the registry cannot hold), ADR-0048 §3.3 (a write addresses exactly one package-keyed row, prefer-local), ADR-0070 TL;DR 1 (the package-less state is no authoring destination, so no text says "bind it to sys_metadata"), and #8907 (every row read in full, never a package-agnostic first match). Head confirmed on the branch before reading.

### ① Derived judgments

1. The one narrowing, right. `saveMetaItem`, type `object`, `mode === 'draft'`, `request.packageId == null`, no `source`, not `package-duplicate` (protocol.ts 22617-22625) now reads `packagelessDraftAddress` and asks `classifyObjectContribution(name, draftAddress.into)` (22626-22629) instead of `(name, request.packageId)`. Over an owner keyed by the `sys_metadata` sentinel, `into` is a package when (a) the active rows are bound to exactly one package Q: `own = active.packageId`, and every draft state returns `into: own` (19296-19303); or (b) no active row is bound and `unboundItemDraftAddress` names the lone package draft (19305-19309; repository 613-620). The answer moves from `200` to `422 OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH`, `packageId` Q, `ownerPackageId` null, thrown before `ensureOverlayIndex` and every `put`, so nothing is written. The question is asked of exactly the row `resolveWriteHead` would write (repository 864-913: one active binding is `targetPackageId`; none reads the draft rows through the same `unboundItemDraftAddress`; two is ambiguous), so the door and the store judge one row, the way the publish-mode save already pairs the door's `packagelessAddress` with the store (22571-22585). D9.9's "refused at the producer, loudly" over a draft no publish can serve (the promote door refuses it since #23704, 24830-24848).
2. The draft address did not move, right. The diff's four hunks are the interface field `strandedDrafts` (2161-2168), one doc row (19736), the new arm (19781-19797) and the door block (22609-22646). `packagelessDraftAddress`, `unboundItemDraftAddress`, `resolveWriteHead`, `put`, the promote door and `deleteMetaItem`'s draft discard (29912-29931) are byte-identical to the merge base. `request.packageId` is not rewritten: `writtenPackage` is a local (22626-22628), so the repository still resolves the binding (#11087).
3. Ambiguous addresses unchanged, right. Two packages' active rows (rows 25-36 with no package named), or two packages' drafts with no package row and no unbound draft (row 11): `packagelessDraftAddress` returns `ambiguous`, `writtenPackage` falls back to `request.packageId` (null), the verdict is `own` (19653-19674), and the repository's `put` throws the same `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` as on main (repository 1011-1019). 409 to 409 is really unchanged.
4. The 200 to 200 cells unchanged, right. `[package-less]` with no draft, the unbound draft, or unbound + Q (rows 1, 3, 7): `unboundItemDraftAddress` answers key null whenever an unbound draft is stored or none at all (616, 619), so `into` is null, the binding reads `''` and the verdict is `own`. The write then lands where it did.
5. Every other door unchanged, right. A save naming a package: `draftAddress` is undefined, `namedNoPackage` is false, so the new arm (19781: `state.mode === 'draft' && state.namedNoPackage && state.at !== 'promote'`) cannot match and the move (draft) and rows-move arms (19804-19827) answer byte for byte as on main (every even matrix row). A publish-mode save: `mode === 'publish'`, `draftAddress` undefined, the address rewrite (22571-22585) and the `namedNoPackage` arm (19798-19803) untouched. The promote door passes `at: 'promote'` (24842-24846), excluded by the arm's third conjunct; the registry write-through (19536-19554) and the boot hydration (30576-30590) pass `at: 'registry'` and no mode, so `state.mode === 'draft'` is false there; a draft save registers nothing, so neither is reached by it anyway. Every type except `object` is behind the guard at 22617. A runtime owner bound to a real package R: `into` is R (one binding), `R === R` reads `own` (19666-19674), no cell changes. A code-package owner: `refusePackagedBaseOverride` (22504) runs above this block, and `isSealedManagedItem` (17351-17354) is `isArtifactBacked && !registryAllowsOverlay(type)`, with `object` outside the regime-O list (17337-17340), so the door answers `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` first, as the CONTROL measured with and without the change.
6. The arm's order and each refused cell's text follow from the code, right. `rows` is `storedPackages`, the active bindings sorted (22635-22637, 19768); `drafts` is `strandedDrafts`, the draft bindings only when no unbound draft is stored (22641-22643, 19789). Steps are each row's `?package=`, then each draft's `?state=draft&package=`, then "send this save again" (19790-19797). Walked per cell from the code, with `deleteMetaItem` naming a package removing that package's row or draft and no other (29921-29931), and the REST door mapping `?state=draft` to `state` and `?package=` to `packageId` (rest-server.ts, the delete route):
   - row Q, no draft (13): `kind: 'none'`, stranded `[]`, one step. After the delete the active rows are `[package-less]` and no draft is stored, so `into` is null, `own`, and `resolveWriteHead` creates the unbound draft.
   - row Q, the unbound draft (15): `key: null, into: Q`, stranded `[]`, one step. After the delete the unbound draft is the address (616) and `put` updates it. The FROM is right too: on main `resolveWriteHead` names Q, finds no Q draft, and the orphan-draft adoption (925-930) stamps the unbound draft into Q.
   - row Q, Q's draft (17): `key: Q, into: Q`, stranded `[Q]`, two steps. H3 holds by the code: with the row gone alone, `unboundItemDraftAddress({[Q], false})` names Q (618-619), the save is refused again as row 5's cell, so the existing `namedNoPackage` text (19800-19803, "then send this save again: it then saves the package-less definition") would be false here. The draft cell is owed its own arm, and the discard naming Q removes Q's draft.
   - row Q, unbound + Q (19): `into: Q`, stranded `[]` (unbound true), one step. After the delete the unbound draft wins (616), `own`, the unbound draft is updated and Q's draft is left stored, as the test's `left` says.
   - row Q, P's draft (21): `kind: 'none', into: Q`, stranded `[P]`, two steps. Needed: after the row's delete alone the lone P draft would be the address.
   - row Q, P + Q (23): `into: Q`, stranded `[P, Q]`, three steps. After the row's delete alone two package drafts answer 409; after P's discard Q's draft is refused; after both, `own`. 416 characters with these ids, prescription first, under the REST 500 bound (19752-19753).
   - no row, Q's draft alone (5) and P's alone (9): `rows` empty, the one discard step, then `own`. The FROM is right: #23657 (c03077e294, below the merge base) sends that save into the lone package draft.
   - States that reach the arm and are not in the matrix: row Q with unbound + P, or unbound + P + Q. `drafts.unbound` is true, stranded is `[]`, the one-step text; after the delete the unbound draft is the address by the same line as row 19. The text is true there. No reachable state with a false text found.
7. Public surface: none beyond the accept set. `UnboundOwnerRefusalState` is a module-private interface (2140, not exported); the error's code, status, `packageId`, `ownerPackageId: null` and `docs` are the existing ones (19836-19842); one new message text is added. No `packages/spec` path, no governed path, no exported declaration added, removed or narrowed.
8. Side effect, acceptable: two more store reads (the active rows and the draft rows) at the door for every object draft save naming no package, before the write. An unprovisioned store reads as no binding, any other read failure propagates (19224-19228, #5532), which the repository's own `find` in `resolveWriteHead` would do one step later anyway.
9. The pins, right for the card: six refused cells (rows 13, 15, 17, 19, 5, 23) assert code, status, both package attributes, the first sentence, the length bound, and nothing written on rows and history, then parse the steps from the text itself (`stepsOf`, which fails on an unknown parameter rather than skipping it), send them in order, boot, and assert rows, registry owner, data-plane and metadata-read labels and both records; two CONTROLs (the package-less owner with no package row or draft writes the unbound draft; a code-package object answers 403). The negative control is the reported ablation (`? draftAddress.into` replaced by `request.packageId`, which is main's line byte for byte): the six refusal pins red, both CONTROLs green. The card asked for the legacy rows across a boot, the CONTROL and a negative control; all three are there.
